sections.title: The letter be
paragraphs: The letter is (be) /be/. Its main sound is a consonant in (bueno) /ˈbwe.no/, which means good. A consonant is a sound made when the mouth blocks or narrows the air. This letter makes two sounds in Spanish.

sections.title: Making the sound
paragraphs: For the first sound, close both lips fully to block the air completely. Turn on your voice and open your lips quickly. For the second sound, bring both lips close together without touching. Let the air flow smoothly through the narrow slit while your voice hums. Touch your throat to feel the strong vibration on both.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: After a pause or after the nasal letters m or n, say the firm sound in (también) /tamˈbjen/. A nasal is a sound where the air goes out through the nose. Between two vowels, say the softer sound in (lobo) /ˈlo.βo/. You also say this softer sound after most other consonants, as in (árbol) /ˈaɾ.βol/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not touch your lower lip to your upper teeth like the v sound in vine. Spanish never uses teeth for this letter. Keep both lips together. Do not block the air completely when the letter sits between two vowels, as in English rabbit. Let the air flow gently through your lips instead.
